long_biography.plain_text:
Neurocrine Biosciences became the platform through which Paul W. Hawran brought financial discipline to experimental drug development. As founding chief financial officer, he oversaw strategic planning, finance, investor relations, staffing, technology and operations while the young biotechnology company moved into public markets.

That breadth reflected training in finance and taxation and earlier large-company planning work. Hawran had grown up on Manhattan’s Lower East Side, the son of parents who emigrated from Ukraine after the Second World War. He later applied the same company-building approach to molecular diagnostics, co-founding Ascendant MDx and leading its women’s-health work as president and chief executive. Life-sciences board appointments extended his role beyond any single company.
